title: Operational Accelerator: Onboarding & Career Skills Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:

This playbook defines Redwood's Operational Accelerator: a combined onboarding, role-progression, and tools-access program designed to reduce time-to-impact for new joiners and provide a repeatable pathway for career growth. It is oriented around 30/60/90 milestones, a lightweight competency matrix, manager and buddy responsibilities, and an explicit tools & benefits checklist to remove operational friction.

Audience:
- New joiners (IC and manager hires)
- Hiring managers and people-ops partners
- Onboarding buddies and mentors
- Team leads responsible for role progression

Goals:
- Standardize first-90-day experience so >80% of hires reach first production change within 45 days.
- Provide transparent promotion indicators tied to measurable outcomes.
- Ensure consistent access to tools (Okta, GitHub, Datadog, Slack, Confluence, Jira, PagerDuty) by day 3.

Owners & escalation:
- Program owner: People Ops Onboarding (owner: Aisha Patel)
- Manager enablement: People Ops Enablement (owner: Marcus Nguyen)
- Tooling & access: IT Access Team (owner: Priya Rao)
- Escalation channel: #onboarding-escalations (Slack) and onboarding@redwood.com

High-level workflow (step-by-step):
1) Offer & pre-boarding (People Ops)
   - Send Welcome Packet (benefits summary, first-week agenda, required compliance training).
   - Provision core accounts (Okta, Google Workspace) and request hardware.
2) Day 0–3: Orientation and access validation
   - Tasks: join Slack, sign up for SSO, clone internal repo, complete security awareness.
   - Access SLA: IT to confirm GitHub/Confluence/Datadog/PagerDuty provisioning within 72 hours; target 95% success.
3) Week 1: Domain ramp and first contribution
   - Assign onboarding buddy for 30 days.
   - Complete role-specific quickstarts (codebase tour, run local server, submit a doc change).
4) Weeks 2–6: Deepening and ownership
   - Participate in at least one cross-team planning meeting.
   - Complete two technical or product learning modules from the Redwood Learning Catalog.
5) Day 45: Manager check-in and readiness review
   - Expected outcome: candidate has made a production-adjacent contribution or owned a small customer-facing task.
6) 60–90 days: Impact & career conversation
   - 90-day review with manager + people-ops to assess competencies and next steps.

Competency Matrix (summary table):
- Technical Craft: Contributes code/architecture for area; demonstrates debugging and testing practices.
- Product Judgment: Understands customer impact and tradeoffs for feature decisions.
- Collaboration: Cross-team communication, effective PRs, constructive reviews.
- Ownership: Delivers end-to-end features or ops enhancements.
- Influence (IC4+): Mentorship, design leadership, measurable improvements in team delivery.

Promotion indicators (what we look for):
- Scope & scale: Breadth of impact beyond single project.
- Autonomy: Consistently delivers with minimal guidance.
- Quality: Ship quality work (low rework, automated tests, monitoring).
- Leadership: Mentors others, leads design reviews, and improves processes.
- Metrics: Demonstrable improvements in KPIs (latency, cost, usage, customer satisfaction).

Manager checklist (first 90 days):
- Before Day 1: Review role onboarding plan and confirm mentor.
- Day 1: 30-minute alignment meeting; set 30/60/90 expectations.
- Weekly: 1:1 touchpoints and blockers log.
- Day 45: Complete readiness form and sign off on first-impact milestone.
- Day 90: Conduct formal 90-day review and update role development plan.

Buddy program (operational details):
- Role: technical and culture partner for 30 days.
- Time commitment: 2–3 hours/week for guided sessions.
- Suggested sessions: code walkthrough, architecture primer, release process demo, benefits intro.

Tools & access checklist (owner: IT Access Team):
- Required by Day 1: Okta, Google Workspace, Slack, Confluence, GitHub read access.
- Required by Day 3: CI/CD pipeline (e.g., GitHub Actions runner access), internal dev cluster, local infra secrets (via Vault).
- Optional within Week 1: Datadog dashboard access, PagerDuty on-call shadowing, Analytics console.
- Verification: Use this CLI snippet to validate access: 
  - curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $OKTA_TOKEN" https://internal-api.redwood.company/me || echo "Okta failed"

Benefits orientation (first-week actions):
- Enroll in health plan: deadline 30 days (People Ops contact: benefits@redwood.com).
- 401(k) auto-enrollment details and contribution guide.
- Flexible work stipend claim instructions (submit via workplace-portal).

Hiring & interview guidance (for hiring managers):
- Interview loop template (recommended): Recruiter screen -> Hiring manager -> Technical assessment -> System design (for senior roles) -> Behavioral -> Offer debrief.
- Calibration: use canned rubrics for Role Competency, with explicit accept/decline thresholds.
- Time-to-hire target: 30 days from recruiter screen to offer for IC roles.

Sample 30/60/90 milestones (IC example):
- 30 days: Local dev environment up, first merged documentation change, understands main product flows.
- 60 days: Small feature delivered to staging, has created or improved test coverage and runbook.
- 90 days: Owns a feature area bug triage, contributed to a cross-team tech discussion, completed career development check-in.

Career-path sketch (engineering example):
- IC1 (New grad/entry): Focus on individual deliverables and learning.
- IC2 (Experienced IC): Solid delivery, effective PRs, starts mentoring interns.
- IC3 (Senior IC): Broad ownership, system design, influences product decisions.
- IC4 (Staff): Cross-team impact, technical leadership, sizable project alphas.
- IC5 (Principal): Company-level technical leadership and long-term roadmap shaping.
- Manager tracks: EM1->EM2->Senior EM with parallel expectations for team growth, hiring, and people development.

Promotion process (practical steps):
1) Candidate prepares promotion packet: 2–3 examples of impact, metrics, and peer feedback.
2) Manager collects at least 3 reviewer reports and confirms timeline.
3) Calibration panel reviews and recommends decision within 30 days.
4) People Ops communicates outcome and next development plan.

Operational metrics (how we measure success):
- Time-to-first-merge (target: median <= 21 days).
- Access SLA (target: 95% of hires have core tools by Day 3).
- 90-day retention target: >= 95% actively employed and in role.
- Manager satisfaction: post-90-day survey score >= 4.2/5.

Templates & artifacts (links and examples):
- 90-day review template: /confluence/templates/90-day-review
- Promotion packet checklist: /confluence/templates/promotion-packet
- Onboarding playbook checklist (CSV): /confluence/downloads/onboard-checklist.csv

Common failure modes & mitigations:
- Missing access: escalate to IT Access Team within 24 hours and run fallback cloud-based lab access.
- No clear 1:1 cadence: manager must schedule weekly 1:1s in first 30 days or People Ops will assign a coaching session.
- Lack of early impact: assign targeted short-milestone projects with clear acceptance criteria.

Appendix: Sample 90-day readiness form (fields):
- Technical accomplishments (bulleted)
- Customer/product impact (numbers or examples)
- Peer feedback summary (2–3 quotes)
- Areas for development and support requests
